spec.name: Daily reversal
spec.notes: Daily reversal on a few hundred names: buy yesterday's losers, sell the winners.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.7, annual return 12%, maximum drawdown 3%.

exhibits.summary: On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is 0.64 against 1.71 in research, a gap of +1.06.
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.71 to 1.71. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.

Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.71 to -2.69 (change -4.40). The strategy already trades a bar after its signal, so this measures how fast the signal fades, not look-ahead.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.71 (as submitted, 10 bps: 1.71); it breaks even at 17.0 bps with daily turnover 0.41.
The strategy made no net profit in research, so there is no P&L to attribute to a year or a regime.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.71 against 1.71 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
The log holds 3 distinct specs; the best of 3 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.22, so the claimed 2.70 becomes 2.48 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The signal has no numeric windows or parameters to perturb.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 4.00 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.02, 95th percentile 0.52).

charges.argument: The strategy fails the holdout test on out-of-sample sealed data, with performance dropping from a research Sharpe of 1.71 to a sealed Sharpe of 0.64.

rebuttals.argument: We concede the selection charge based on EX-1, which demonstrates a significant performance drop in the sealed holdout period from 1.71 to 0.64.

verdict.opinion: The selection charge is sustained by damaging exhibit EX-1 (holdout_test), which reveals a substantial drop in Sharpe ratio from 1.71 in research down to 0.64 on the sealed holdout period. While the signal still achieves a positive Sharpe ratio out-of-sample and shows genuine statistical significance in placebo testing (EX-9), the significant performance degradation indicates notable overfitting to the research sample. Given the mixed evidence—where the core edge appears real but out-of-sample efficacy is considerably weaker than claimed—real capital deployment is not justified at this time. Capital allocation is set to 0 and the strategy is relegated to paper trading.
